newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian anthrax quarantine zone widened.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian anthrax quarantine zone widened.

text.p: A quarantine zone surrounding an Australian anthrax outbreak has been widened after the discovery of two outlying cases of the disease, officials said on Monday.

The number of deaths has also risen, to 160 cattle and three sheep, while 79 properties have been confirmed to have anthrax, a spokeswoman for the Victorian state Department of Natural Resources and Environment said.
However, the spread of the disease appeared to be slowing, said the department's chief veterinary officer Dr Andrew Turner.
"It seems to be going down and staying down, and that's good news," Turner told Reuters from Tatura in Victoria.
An additional 50,000 doses of vaccine arrived in Australia on Monday from the United States.

Department staff have vaccinated 45,000 cattle and 1,700 sheep on 321 properties since the outbreak was discovered on January 26. Turner said authorities currently planned to vaccinate about 60,000 cattle in total.
Australian officials have repeatedly stated that anthrax poses no threat to consumers of dairy products because of processing and other safeguards.
Australia exports about A$1.8 billion worth of processed dairy products a year, to Europe, the Middle East and Asia.
The anthrax outbreak is in the Goulburn Valley area of Victoria between Tatura and Stanhope. The area supplies about 30 percent of Australia's dairy products.
Anthrax is a bacterial infection which causes rapid death in cattle, sheep and goats when they eat contaminated soil or feed and is propagated by hot, humid weather, especially after rain.
It rarely affects humans although one meat industry worker has been infected during the latest outbreak, probably through a scratch or cut.
